right:<br/><span style="font-size:85%;">(Top Row)</span> <a href="/wiki/Patrick_McHale_(artist)" title="Patrick McHale (artist)">Patrick McHale</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kent_Osborne" title="Kent Osborne">Kent Osborne</a><br/><span style="font-size:85%;">(Bottom Row)</span> <a href="/wiki/Rebecca_Sugar" title="Rebecca Sugar">Rebecca Sugar</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ian_Jones-Quartey" title="Ian Jones-Quartey">Ian Jones-Quartey</a>.</div></div></div></div>
<p>Several former crew members who worked on <i>Adventure Time</i> have gone on to create their own series, including Patrick McHale (a former storyline writer, storyboard artist, and creative director who went on to create <i><a href="/wiki/Over_the_Garden_Wall" title="Over the Garden Wall">Over the Garden Wall</a></i>),<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-180"><a href="#cite_note-180"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>176<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> J.G. Quintel (a former storyboard artist who went on to create <i><a href="/wiki/Regular_Show" title="Regular Show">Regular Show</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Close_Enough" title="Close Enough">Close Enough</a></i>), <a href="/wiki/Peter_Browngardt" title="Peter Browngardt">Pete Browngardt</a> (a former storyboard artist who went on to create <i><a href="/wiki/Secret_Mountain_Fort_Awesome" title="Secret Mountain Fort Awesome">Secret Mountain Fort Awesome</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Uncle_Grandpa" title="Uncle Grandpa">Uncle Grandpa</a></i>, and <i><a href="/wiki/Looney_Tunes_Cartoons" title="Looney Tunes Cartoons">Looney Tunes Cartoons</a></i>),<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-181"><a href="#cite_note-181"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>177<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Rebecca Sugar (a former storyboard artist who went on to create <i><a href="/wiki/Steven_Universe" title="Steven Universe">Steven Universe</a></i>),<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-182"><a href="#cite_note-182"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>178<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Ian Jones-Quartey (a former storyboard revisionist and supervisor who went on to create <i><a href="/wiki/OK_K.O.!_Let%27s_Be_Heroes" title="OK K.O.! Let's Be Heroes">OK K.O.! Let's Be Heroes</a></i>),<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-183"><a href="#cite_note-183"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>179<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Skyler Page (a former storyboard artist who went on to create <i><a href="/wiki/Clarence_(American_TV_series)" title="Clarence (American TV series)">Clarence</a></i>),<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-Milligan_2012_184-0"><a href="#cite_note-Milligan_2012-184"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>180<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Julia Pott (a former storyline writer who went on to create <i><a href="/wiki/Summer_Camp_Island" title="Summer Camp Island">Summer Camp Island</a></i>),<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-185"><a href="#cite_note-185"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>181<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Kent Osborne (the show's former head story writer who went on to create <i><a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Cat_Agent" title="Cat Agent">Cat Agent</a></i>),<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-186"><a href="#cite_note-186"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>182<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-187"><a href="#cite_note-187"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>183<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and Elizabeth Ito (a former storyboard artist and supervising director who created <i><a href="/wiki/City_of_Ghosts_(TV_series)" title="City of Ghosts (TV series)">City of Ghosts</a></i> for <a href="/wiki/Netflix" title="Netflix">Netflix</a>).<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-188"><a href="#cite_note-188"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>184<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Heidi MacDonald of <i>Slate</i> has argued that the scouting of indie comic creators employed by <i>Adventure Time</i> (as well as several other Cartoon Network and Nickelodeon series) has led to an "animation gold rush" in which major studios are actively seeking under-the-radar talent for their shows, with her article surmising that "your favorite brilliant indie cartoonist is probably storyboarding for <i>Adventure Time</i>".<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-slateinfluence_189-0"><a href="#cite_note-slateinfluence-189"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>185<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> MacDonald also pointed out that <i>Adventure Time</i> has influenced the tone of modern comics, noting:
</p>
<blockquote><p>If anything, walking around [comic] shows like <a href="/wiki/Small_Press_Expo" title="Small Press Expo">SPX</a>, I've noticed something of an <i>Adventure Time</i> track among many of the small press comics now coming out: Where once young cartoonists overwhelmingly produced gloomy masculine self-absorption and misanthropy in the tradition of <a href="/wiki/Daniel_Clowes" title="Daniel Clowes">Daniel Clowes</a> or <a href="/wiki/Chris_Ware" title="Chris Ware">Chris Ware</a>, these days many booths feature fantasy epics with colorful characters and invented worlds heavy on the talking animals. It shouldn't be surprising that up-and-coming cartoonists are absorbing the <i>Adventure Time</i> aesthetic. A 20-year-old making comics now could have been watching the show since she was 15, after all.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-slateinfluence_189-1"><a href="#cite_note-slateinfluence-189"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>185<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></p></blockquote>
<p>In an interview with <i><a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Paper_Magazine" title="Paper Magazine">Paste</a></i> magazine, Rebecca Sugar explained that working on <i>Adventure Time</i> and connecting with indie and underground comic artists who worked on the show (like Ward, McHale and Muto) was a creative game-changer, as they told her to do what she would do when drawing comics and to not hold anything back. She argued that many of the recent developments in animation were inspired by what the show was able to do by being "very artist-driven" and allowing independent comic artists to have a major say in the direction of episodes.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-Moen_94-2"><a href="#cite_note-Moen-94"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>90<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Academic_interest">Academic interest</h3></div>
<p><i>Adventure Time</i> has attracted academic interest for its presentation of gender and <a href="/wiki/Gender_role" title="Gender role">gender roles</a>. Emma A. Jane, an academic from the <a href="/wiki/University_of_New_South_Wales" title="University of New South Wales">University of New South Wales</a> in <a href="/wiki/Sydney" title="Sydney">Sydney</a>, Australia, wrote that while the two main characters are male and many episodes involve them engaging in violent acts to save princesses, "Finn and Jake are [nevertheless] part of an expansive ensemble cast of characters who are anything but stereotypical and who populate a program which subverts many traditional gender-related paradigms".<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-childrenmedia_190-0"><a href="#cite_note-childrenmedia-190"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>186<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> She said the show features "roughly equal numbers of female and male characters in a protagonist, antagonist, and minor roles"; includes characters with no fixed gender; uses "gendered 'design elements'" such as eyelashes and hair to illustrate character traits rather than gender; equally distributes traits regardless of gender; privileges found, adoptive families or <a href="/wiki/Family#Extended_family" title="Family">extended families</a>; frames gender in ways that suggest it is <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Genderfluid" title="Genderfluid">fluid</a>, and features elements of <a href="/wiki/Queer" title="Queer">queer</a> and <a href="/wiki/Transgender" title="Transgender">transgender</a> sub-text.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-childrenmedia_190-1"><a href="#cite_note-childrenmedia-190"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>186<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Carolyn Leslie, writing in <i><a href="/wiki/Screen_(journal)" title="Screen (journal)">Screen</a></i>, agrees, saying, "despite having two male leads, <i>Adventure Time</i> is particularly strong when it comes to questioning and challenging gender stereotypes".<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-lesliegener_191-0"><a href="#cite_note-lesliegener-191"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>187<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> She uses Princess Bubblegum, BMO, and Fionna and Cake as examples of characters who refuse to be readily categorized and genderized.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-lesliegener_191-1"><a href="#cite_note-lesliegener-191"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>187<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The first non-fiction book to scholarly study the series was <i><a class="extiw" href="//archive.org/details/adventuretimephi0000unse" title="iarchive:adventuretimephi0000unse">Adventure Time and Philosophy</a></i> (2015), edited by Nicolas Michaud. Published by <a href="/wiki/Open_Court_Publishing_Company" title="Open Court Publishing Company">Open Court Publishing Company</a>, this work considers <i>Adventure Time</i> from a variety of angles, using the show as a way to explore different philosophical ideas.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-192"><a href="#cite_note-192"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>188<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In July 2020, independent scholar Paul A. Thomas released a book entitled <i>Exploring the Land of Ooo</i> that documented the show's production history; an expanded and updated version of the book was released in 2023 by the <a href="/wiki/University_Press_of_Mississippi" title="University Press of Mississippi">University Press of Mississippi</a>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-paul_26-5"><a href="#cite_note-paul-26"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>22<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Fandom">Fandom</h3></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a class="mw-file-description" href="/wiki/File:Lumpy_Space_Princess_and_Princess_Bubblegum.jpg"><img alt="The image depicts two individuals dressed up as characters from the show" class="mw-file-element" data-file-height="3162" data-file-width="4743" decoding="async" height="167" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Lumpy_Space_Princess_and_Princess_Bubblegum.jpg/250px-Lumpy_Space_Princess_and_Princess_Bubblegum.jpg" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Lumpy_Space_Princess_and_Princess_Bubblegum.jpg/500px-Lumpy_Space_Princess_and_Princess_Bubblegum.jpg 1.5x" width="250"/></a><figcaption><i>Adventure Time</i> fans <a href="/wiki/Cosplay" title="Cosplay">cosplaying</a> as Princess Bubblegum (<i>left</i>) and Lumpy Space Princess (<i>right</i>)</figcaption></figure>
<p>Since its debut, <i>Adventure Time</i> has developed a strong following among children, teenagers, and adults; according to <i>A.V. Club</i> critic Noel Murray, fans are drawn to <i>Adventure Time</i> because of "the show's silly humor, imaginative stories, and richly populated world".<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-avclubinterview_35-4"><a href="#cite_note-avclubinterview-35"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>31<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> While the show is often described as having a <a href="/wiki/Cult_following" title="Cult following">cult following</a>,<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-rollingstoneinterview_30-2"><a href="#cite_note-rollingstoneinterview-30"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>26<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-193"><a href="#cite_note-193"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>189<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Eric Kohn of <i>IndieWire</i> said that the series has "started to look like one of the biggest television phenomenons of the decade".<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-fandomkohn_194-0"><a href="#cite_note-fandomkohn-194"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>190<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> According to Alex Heigl of <i><a href="/wiki/People_(magazine)" title="People (magazine)">People</a></i> magazine, "The show's <a href="/wiki/Fandom" title="Fandom">fandom</a> is especially Internet-savvy as well, with huge communities on <a href="/wiki/Reddit" title="Reddit">Reddit</a>, <a href="/wiki/Imgur" title="Imgur">Imgur</a> and <a href="/wiki/Tumblr" title="Tumblr">Tumblr</a>, who swap <a href="/wiki/GIF" title="GIF">GIFs</a>, fan art and theories with fervent regularity".<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-195"><a href="#cite_note-195"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>191<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 2016, a study by <i><a href="/wiki/The_New_York_Times" title="The New York Times">The New York Times</a></i> of the 50 TV shows with the most <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Facebook_Like" title="Facebook Like">Facebook Likes</a> found that <i>Adventure Time</i> "is the most popular show among the young in our data—just over two-thirds of 'likes' come from viewers [aged] 18–24".<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-katz20161227_196-0"><a href="#cite_note-katz20161227-196"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>192<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The show is popular at <a href="/wiki/Fan_convention" title="Fan convention">fan conventions</a>, such as <a href="/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con" title="San Diego Comic-Con">San Diego Comic-Con</a>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-fandomkohn_194-1"><a href="#cite_note-fandomkohn-194"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>190<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Reporter Emma-Lee Moss said, "This year's [2014] Comic-Con schedule reflected <i>Adventure Time</i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">'</span>s growing success, with several screenings [as well as] a dramatic reading with the show's voice talent".<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-emmalee_197-0"><a href="#cite_note-emmalee-197"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>193<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The show is also popular with <a href="/wiki/Cosplay" title="Cosplay">cosplayers</a>, or <a href="/wiki/Performance_art" title="Performance art">performance artists</a> who wear costumes and fashion accessories to represent characters from the <i>Adventure Time</i> universe. Moss wrote, "Looking into the crowd, it was clear that [Finn's] distinctive blue shirt and white hat were being mirrored by hundreds of Cosplayers, male and female".<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-emmalee_197-1"><a href="#cite_note-emmalee-197"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>193<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In an interview, Olivia Olson (who voices the character Marceline) said, "Literally, anywhere you look, anywhere in your range, you're going to see at least two people dressed up like Finn. It's crazy".<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-marysueinterview_198-0"><a href="#cite_note-marysueinterview-198"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>194<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Accolades">Accolades</h3></div>
<link href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1236090951" rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style"/><div class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" role="note">Main article: <a href="/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_the_Adventure_Time_franchise" title="List of awards and nominations received by the Adventure Time franchise">List of awards and nominations received by the <i>Adventure Time</i> franchise</a></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Related_media">Related media</h2></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Spin-offs">Spin-offs</h3></div>
<link href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1236090951" rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style"/><div class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" role="note">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Adventure_Time:_Distant_Lands" title="Adventure Time: Distant Lands"><i>Adventure Time: Distant Lands</i></a> and <a href="/wiki/Adventure_Time:_Fionna_and_Cake" title="Adventure Time: Fionna and Cake"><i>Adventure Time: Fionna and Cake</i></a></div>
<p>On October 23, 2019, Cartoon Network announced that four hour-long specials—collectively titled <i><a href="/wiki/Adventure_Time:_Distant_Lands" title="Adventure Time: Distant Lands">Adventure Time: Distant Lands</a></i>—would air on <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/HBO_Max" title="HBO Max">HBO Max</a>. The specials aired in 2020 and 2021. On August 17, 2021, it was announced that a second spin-off, <i><a href="/wiki/Adventure_Time:_Fionna_and_Cake" title="Adventure Time: Fionna and Cake">Adventure Time: Fionna and Cake</a></i>, focusing on the gender-swapped <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Fionna_Campbell_and_Cake_the_Cat" title="Fionna Campbell and Cake the Cat">Fionna and Cake</a> characters, had been ordered by HBO Max.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-199"><a href="#cite_note-199"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>195<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On June 12, 2024, it was revealed that two additional spin-offs, entitled <i>Adventure Time: Side Quests</i> and <i>Adventure Time: Heyo BMO</i>, had also been greenlit by Cartoon Network Studios.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-movie-spinoff_200-0"><a href="#cite_note-movie-spinoff-200"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>196<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Comic_books">Comic books</h3></div>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a class="mw-file-description" href="/wiki/File:Comic_adventure_time.JPG"><img class="mw-file-element" data-file-height="3456" data-file-width="4608" decoding="async" height="225" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Comic_adventure_time.JPG/330px-Comic_adventure_time.JPG" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Comic_adventure_time.JPG/500px-Comic_adventure_time.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Comic_adventure_time.JPG/960px-Comic_adventure_time.JPG 2x" width="300"/></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Ryan_North" title="Ryan North">Ryan North</a> (<i>third from the left</i>) along with other <i>Adventure Time</i> comics crew in 2015</figcaption></figure>
<p>On November 19, 2011, <a href="/wiki/Boom!_Studios#KaBoom!" title="Boom! Studios">KaBoom! Studios</a> announced plans for an <i>Adventure Time</i> comic book series written by independent webcomic creator <a href="/wiki/Ryan_North" title="Ryan North">Ryan North</a>, who wrote the series <i><a href="/wiki/Dinosaur_Comics" title="Dinosaur Comics">Dinosaur Comics</a></i>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-201"><a href="#cite_note-201"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>197<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-202"><a href="#cite_note-202"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>198<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The series launched on February 8, 2012, with art by Shelli Paroline and Braden Lamb.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-203"><a href="#cite_note-203"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>199<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-204"><a href="#cite_note-204"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>200<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In October 2014, it was revealed that North had left the comic series after three years. His duties were assumed by <a href="/wiki/Christopher_Hastings" title="Christopher Hastings">Christopher Hastings</a>, the creator of <i><a href="/wiki/The_Adventures_of_Dr._McNinja" title="The Adventures of Dr. McNinja">The Adventures of Dr. McNinja</a></i>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-205"><a href="#cite_note-205"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>201<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This comic book line ended in April 2018 with its seventy-fifth issue, which North returned to co-write.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-206"><a href="#cite_note-206"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>202<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>After the success of the original comic book line, several spin-off mini-series were launched. Some of the comic series are as follows:
</p>

<tr>
<td><i>Adventure Time: Marceline and the Scream Queens</i></td>
<td>Meredith Gran</td>
<td>July 11, 2012</td>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Other_literature">Other literature</h3></div>
<p>Other <i>Adventure Time</i>-themed books have also been released. <i>The Adventure Time Encyclopaedia</i>, published on July 22, 2013, was written by comedian <a href="/wiki/Martin_Olson" title="Martin Olson">Martin Olson</a>, father of Olivia Olson and the voice of recurring character Hunson Abadeer.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-240"><a href="#cite_note-240"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>235<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This was followed by <i>Adventure Time: The Enchiridion &amp; Marcy's Super Secret Scrapbook!!!</i>, which was released on October 6, 2015. Written by Martin and Olivia Olson, it is presented as a combination of the <i>Enchiridion</i> and Marceline's secret diary.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-241"><a href="#cite_note-241"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>236<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> An official <i>Art of ...</i> book, titled <i>The Art of Ooo</i> was published on October 14, 2014. It contains interviews with cast and crew members and opens with an introduction by filmmaker <a href="/wiki/Guillermo_del_Toro" title="Guillermo del Toro">Guillermo del Toro</a>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-artooo_18-15"><a href="#cite_note-artooo-18"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Two volumes with collections of the show's <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Title_card" title="Title card">title cards</a> have also been released,<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-242"><a href="#cite_note-242"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>237<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-243"><a href="#cite_note-243"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>238<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> as has a cookbook with recipes inspired by the show,<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-244"><a href="#cite_note-244"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>239<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and a series of prose novels published under the header "Epic Tales from <i>Adventure Time</i>" (which includes <i>The Untamed Scoundrel</i>, <i>Queen of Rogues</i>, <i>The Lonesome Outlaw</i>, and <i>The Virtue of Ardor</i>, all of which were published under the <a href="/wiki/Pseudonym" title="Pseudonym">pseudonym</a> "T. T. MacDangereuse").<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-245"><a href="#cite_note-245"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>240<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-246"><a href="#cite_note-246"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>241<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-247"><a href="#cite_note-247"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>242<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-248"><a href="#cite_note-248"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>243<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Video_games">Video games</h3></div>
<p>The series has spawned several major video game releases. The first game based on the series, <i><a href="/wiki/Adventure_Time:_Hey_Ice_King!_Why%27d_You_Steal_Our_Garbage%3F!!" title="Adventure Time: Hey Ice King! Why'd You Steal Our Garbage?!!">Adventure Time: Hey Ice King! Why'd You Steal Our Garbage?!!</a></i>, was announced by Pendleton Ward on his <a href="/wiki/Twitter" title="Twitter">Twitter</a> account in March 2012.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-249"><a href="#cite_note-249"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>244<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The game was developed by <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/WayForward_Technologies" title="WayForward Technologies">WayForward Technologies</a> for <a href="/wiki/Nintendo_DS" title="Nintendo DS">Nintendo DS</a> and <a href="/wiki/Nintendo_3DS" title="Nintendo 3DS">Nintendo 3DS</a>, and was released by <a href="/wiki/D3_Publisher" title="D3 Publisher">D3 Publisher</a> on November 20, 2012.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-250"><a href="#cite_note-250"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>245<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-251"><a href="#cite_note-251"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>246<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A year later, the game <i><a href="/wiki/Adventure_Time:_Explore_the_Dungeon_Because_I_Don%27t_Know!" title="Adventure Time: Explore the Dungeon Because I Don't Know!">Adventure Time: Explore the Dungeon Because I Don't Know!</a></i>, which follows Finn and Jake as they strive "to save the Candy Kingdom by exploring the mysterious Secret Royal Dungeon deep below the Land of Ooo",<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-newgameign_252-0"><a href="#cite_note-newgameign-252"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>247<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> was released in November 2013.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-newgameign_252-1"><a href="#cite_note-newgameign-252"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>247<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On November 18, 2014, <i><a href="/wiki/Adventure_Time:_The_Secret_of_the_Nameless_Kingdom" title="Adventure Time: The Secret of the Nameless Kingdom">Adventure Time: The Secret of the Nameless Kingdom</a></i> was released for Nintendo 3DS, <a href="/wiki/Xbox_360" title="Xbox 360">Xbox 360</a>, <a href="/wiki/PlayStation_3" title="PlayStation 3">PlayStation 3</a>, <a href="/wiki/PlayStation_Vita" title="PlayStation Vita">PlayStation Vita</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Microsoft_Windows" title="Microsoft Windows">Microsoft Windows</a>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-253"><a href="#cite_note-253"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>248<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In October 2015, the fourth major <i>Adventure Time</i> video game, titled <i><a href="/wiki/Adventure_Time:_Finn_%26_Jake_Investigations" title="Adventure Time: Finn &amp; Jake Investigations">Finn &amp; Jake Investigations</a></i>, was released for 3DS, Windows and other consoles. It is the first in the series to feature full 3D graphics.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-IGNcites_254-0"><a href="#cite_note-IGNcites-254"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>249<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Another game, <i><a href="/wiki/Adventure_Time:_Pirates_of_the_Enchiridion" title="Adventure Time: Pirates of the Enchiridion">Adventure Time: Pirates of the Enchiridion</a></i>, was released for the <a href="/wiki/PlayStation_4" title="PlayStation 4">PlayStation 4</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nintendo_Switch" title="Nintendo Switch">Nintendo Switch</a>, Windows, and <a href="/wiki/Xbox_One" title="Xbox One">Xbox One</a> in July 2018.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-255"><a href="#cite_note-255"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>250<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The game was published by Outright Games, developed by <a href="/wiki/Climax_Studios" title="Climax Studios">Climax Studios</a>, and features the show's original cast.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-pirates_ench_256-0"><a href="#cite_note-pirates_ench-256"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>251<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> That game won the award for "Performance in a Comedy, Lead" with John DiMaggio at the National Academy of Video Game Trade Reviewers Awards, in which Jeremy Shada was also nominated for the same category.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-257"><a href="#cite_note-257"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>252<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-258"><a href="#cite_note-258"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>253<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Various other minor video games have also been released. Several, including <i>Legends of Ooo</i>, <i>Fionna Fights</i>, <i>Beemo – Adventure Time</i>, and <i>Ski Safari: Adventure Time</i>, have been released on the <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/App_Store_(iOS)" title="App Store (iOS)">iOS App Store</a>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-259"><a href="#cite_note-259"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>254<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A game titled <i>Finn &amp; Jake's Quest</i> was released on April 11, 2014, on <a href="/wiki/Steam_(service)" title="Steam (service)">Steam</a>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-260"><a href="#cite_note-260"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>255<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Cartoon Network also released a multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) game titled <i>Adventure Time: Battle Party</i> on Cartoon Network's official site, on June 23, 2014.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-261"><a href="#cite_note-261"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>256<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In April 2015, two downloadable content packs for <i><a href="/wiki/LittleBigPlanet_3" title="LittleBigPlanet 3">LittleBigPlanet 3</a></i> on PlayStation 3 and PlayStation 4 were released; one contained <i>Adventure Time</i> costumes, while the other contained a level kit with decorations, stickers, music, objects, a background, and a bonus Fionna costume.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-262"><a href="#cite_note-262"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>257<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A <a href="/wiki/Virtual_reality" title="Virtual reality">virtual reality</a> (VR) game entitled <i>Adventure Time: Magic Man's Head Games</i> was also released to <a href="/wiki/Oculus_Rift" title="Oculus Rift">Oculus Rift</a>, <a href="/wiki/HTC_Vive" title="HTC Vive">HTC Vive</a>, and <a href="/wiki/PlayStation_VR" title="PlayStation VR">PlayStation VR</a>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-263"><a href="#cite_note-263"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>258<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A second VR game, entitled <i>Adventure Time: I See Ooo</i>, was released on September 29, 2016.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-264"><a href="#cite_note-264"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>259<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In that same month, <i>Adventure Time</i> characters were added to the <i><a href="/wiki/Lego_Dimensions" title="Lego Dimensions">Lego Dimensions</a></i> game.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-265"><a href="#cite_note-265"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>260<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-266"><a href="#cite_note-266"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>261<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Finn and Jake became playable characters in the video game <i><a href="/wiki/Cartoon_Network:_Battle_Crashers" title="Cartoon Network: Battle Crashers">Cartoon Network: Battle Crashers</a></i> which was released for the Nintendo 3DS, PlayStation 4, Xbox One on November 8, 2016 and the Nintendo Switch on October 31, 2017.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-267"><a href="#cite_note-267"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>262<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-268"><a href="#cite_note-268"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>263<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Finn, Jake, Banana Guard, and Marceline are playable characters in the <a href="/wiki/Platform_fighter" title="Platform fighter">platform fighter</a> <i><a href="/wiki/MultiVersus" title="MultiVersus">MultiVersus</a></i>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-269"><a href="#cite_note-269"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>264<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-270"><a href="#cite_note-270"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>265<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Film">Film</h3></div>
<p>In February 2015, it was reported that a theatrical <i>Adventure Time</i> film was being developed by <a href="/wiki/Cartoon_Network_Studios" title="Cartoon Network Studios">Cartoon Network Studios</a>, <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Frederator_Films" title="Frederator Films">Frederator Films</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vertigo_Entertainment" title="Vertigo Entertainment">Vertigo Entertainment</a>, and <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Warner_Animation_Group" title="Warner Animation Group">Warner Animation Group</a>. According to reports, the film would be executive-produced and written by Pendleton Ward, and produced by <a href="/wiki/Roy_Lee" title="Roy Lee">Roy Lee</a> and <a href="/wiki/Chris_McKay" title="Chris McKay">Chris McKay</a>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-271"><a href="#cite_note-271"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>266<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-272"><a href="#cite_note-272"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>267<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In October 2015, series producer Adam Muto confirmed that series creator Pendleton Ward was "working on the premise" for the film, but that there was "nothing official to announce yet".<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-273"><a href="#cite_note-273"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>268<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On July 22, 2018, Muto noted that "an [<i>Adventure Time</i>] movie was never officially announced".<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-274"><a href="#cite_note-274"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>269<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On August 31, 2018, Muto said the finale of the show would not affect a potential movie, nor would the finale lead directly into a film. He also noted that "all the lore and stuff would not work for a first time viewer", suggesting that the film would have to hold well on its own to be successful.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-275"><a href="#cite_note-275"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>270<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>However, on June 12, 2024, during the <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Annecy_Animation_Festival" title="Annecy Animation Festival">Annecy Animation Festival</a>, it was announced that an <i>Adventure Time</i> movie was in development, with Rebecca Sugar, Adam Muto, and Patrick McHale all involved in the project.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-movie-spinoff_200-1"><a href="#cite_note-movie-spinoff-200"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>196<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Other_appearances">Other appearances</h3></div>
<link href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1236090951" rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style"/><div class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" role="note">This is a <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Lists#Dynamic_lists" title="Wikipedia:WikiProject Lists">dynamic list</a> and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. You can help by <a href="/wiki/Special:EditPage/Adventure_Time" title="Special:EditPage/Adventure Time">adding missing items</a> with <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources" title="Wikipedia:Reliable sources">reliable sources</a>.</div>
<p>A variety of officially licensed merchandise—including action figures, role-playing toys, bedding, dishware, and various other products—have been released.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-276"><a href="#cite_note-276"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>271<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Since the dramatic increase in popularity of the series, many graphic T-shirts have been officially licensed through popular clothing retailers.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-277"><a href="#cite_note-277"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>272<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-278"><a href="#cite_note-278"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>273<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-threadless_279-0"><a href="#cite_note-threadless-279"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>274<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Pendleton Ward hosted T-shirt designing contests on the websites of both We Love Fine and <a href="/wiki/Threadless" title="Threadless">Threadless</a>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-threadless_279-1"><a href="#cite_note-threadless-279"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>274<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-280"><a href="#cite_note-280"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>275<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Other shirts can be purchased directly from Cartoon Network's store.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-281"><a href="#cite_note-281"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>276<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A <a href="/wiki/Collectible_card_game" title="Collectible card game">collectible card game</a> called <i>Card Wars</i>, inspired by the fourth-season episode of the same name, has been released.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-282"><a href="#cite_note-282"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>277<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On March 11, 2016, it was announced by <a href="/wiki/Lego" title="Lego">Lego</a> via <a href="/wiki/Lego_Ideas" title="Lego Ideas">Lego Ideas</a> that an official <i>Adventure Time</i> Lego set from an idea by site user, aBetterMonkey, had met voting qualifications and was approved to be produced in cooperation with Cartoon Network.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-283"><a href="#cite_note-283"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>278<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-284"><a href="#cite_note-284"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>279<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The set was released in January 2017.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-285"><a href="#cite_note-285"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>280<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On July 21, 2013, <a href="/wiki/Taiwan_High_Speed_Rail" title="Taiwan High Speed Rail">Taiwan High Speed Rail</a> and the <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Cartoon_Network_(Asian_TV_channel)#Taiwan" title="Cartoon Network (Asian TV channel)">Taiwan branch of Cartoon Network</a> worked together on a project called "Cartoon Express" (<span lang="zh">歡樂卡通列車</span>). The entire train was covered with characters from various Cartoon Network shows (including <i><a href="/wiki/The_Amazing_World_of_Gumball" title="The Amazing World of Gumball">The Amazing World of Gumball</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/The_Powerpuff_Girls" title="The Powerpuff Girls">The Powerpuff Girls</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Ben_10" title="Ben 10">Ben 10</a></i>, and <i><a href="/wiki/Regular_Show" title="Regular Show">Regular Show</a></i>), and the two sides of the train is painted with Finn and Jake respectively.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-286"><a href="#cite_note-286"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>281<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-287"><a href="#cite_note-287"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>282<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-288"><a href="#cite_note-288"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>283<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Throughout the project, there were over 1,400 runs of the train and over 1.3 million passengers were transported. Near the end, the Taiwan High Speed Rail also sold postcards as souvenirs for sale since August 23, 2014, and the project eventually ended on September 9, 2014.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-289"><a href="#cite_note-289"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>284<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-290"><a href="#cite_note-290"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>285<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In addition, Cartoon Network established a <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Waterpark" title="Waterpark">waterpark</a> named <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Cartoon_Network_Amazone" title="Cartoon Network Amazone">Cartoon Network Amazone</a> in <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Chonburi_Province" title="Chonburi Province">Chonburi</a>, Thailand; it opened on October 3, 2014.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-291"><a href="#cite_note-291"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>286<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Promoting the waterpark, <a href="/wiki/Thai_Smile" title="Thai Smile">Thai Smile</a> painted Finn, Jake, Princess Bubblegum and Marceline on the planes.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-292"><a href="#cite_note-292"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>287<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<p>"<a href="/wiki/Leela_and_the_Genestalk" title="Leela and the Genestalk">Leela and the Genestalk</a>", an episode from the <a href="/wiki/Futurama_season_7" title="Futurama season 7">seventh season</a> of the animated <a href="/wiki/Comedy_Central" title="Comedy Central">Comedy Central</a> program <i><a href="/wiki/Futurama" title="Futurama">Futurama</a></i>, features a cameo of Finn and Jake, with DiMaggio (who voices <a href="/wiki/Bender_(Futurama)" title="Bender (Futurama)">Bender</a> in <i>Futurama</i>) reprising his role as Jake for the appearance.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-293"><a href="#cite_note-293"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>288<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Similarly, the <a href="/wiki/The_Simpsons_season_28" title="The Simpsons season 28">twenty-eighth season</a> premiere of the <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Fox_Network" title="Fox Network">Fox</a> series <i>The Simpsons</i>, entitled "<a href="/wiki/Monty_Burns%27_Fleeing_Circus" title="Monty Burns' Fleeing Circus">Monty Burns' Fleeing Circus</a>", includes a couch gag that parodies the title sequence to <i>Adventure Time</i>, complete with Pendleton Ward himself singing a spoof of the <i>Adventure Time</i> theme song. According to <a href="/wiki/Al_Jean" title="Al Jean">Al Jean</a>, the executive producer of <i>The Simpsons</i>, "[The couch gag] was the brain child of Mike Anderson, our supervising director ... It's a really beautiful, elaborate crossover".<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-294"><a href="#cite_note-294"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>289<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On the Portuguese talk show <i><a href="/wiki/5_Para_A_Meia-Noite" title="5 Para A Meia-Noite">5 Para A Meia-Noite</a></i>, the humorist Eduardo Madeira, who portrayed a hater called Osório, used Princess Bubblegum and Marceline to mock the <a href="/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2018" title="Eurovision Song Contest 2018">Eurovision Song Contest 2018</a>'s Portuguese contestants, <a href="/wiki/Cl%C3%A1udia_Pascoal" title="Cláudia Pascoal">Cláudia Pascoal</a> and <a href="/wiki/Isaura_(singer)" title="Isaura (singer)">Isaura</a>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-295"><a href="#cite_note-295"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>290<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-296"><a href="#cite_note-296"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>291<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In the 2016 horror film <i><a href="/wiki/Better_Watch_Out" title="Better Watch Out">Better Watch Out</a></i>, the two boys in the film, Luke the antagonist and his friend Garrett, are fans of the series, and after subduing Luke's babysitter and using drugs and alcohol, the two boys play <a href="/wiki/Fuck,_marry,_kill" title="Fuck, marry, kill">Fuck, Marry, Kill</a> using the "<i>Adventure Time</i> chicks" as options. Luke says that he would, "[f]uck Princess Bubblegum," to which Garrett replies, "Not Marceline?" Luke then gives reasons for his choice.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-297"><a href="#cite_note-297"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>292<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-298"><a href="#cite_note-298"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>293<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Notes">Notes</h2></div>

<li id="cite_note-note1-5"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-note1_5-0">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text"><a href="/wiki/Larry_Leichliter" title="Larry Leichliter">Larry Leichliter</a> served as director until the fifth-season episode "<a href="/wiki/Bad_Little_Boy" title="Bad Little Boy">Bad Little Boy</a>". After this episode, the term was phased out in favor of "supervising director",<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-directorquestion_4-0"><a href="#cite_note-directorquestion-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and the following have served in this role: <a href="/wiki/Nate_Cash" title="Nate Cash">Nate Cash</a> (season 5), <a href="/wiki/Adam_Muto" title="Adam Muto">Adam Muto</a> (seasons 5–9), Elizabeth Ito (seasons 5–9), <a href="/wiki/Kent_Osborne" title="Kent Osborne">Kent Osborne</a> (season 6), Andres Salaff (seasons 6–8), <a href="/wiki/Cole_Sanchez" title="Cole Sanchez">Cole Sanchez</a> (seasons 6, 8–10), and Diana Lafyatis (season 10). Guest directors for the series have included: <a href="/wiki/David_OReilly_(artist)" title="David OReilly (artist)">David OReilly</a> ("<a href="/wiki/A_Glitch_Is_a_Glitch" title="A Glitch Is a Glitch">A Glitch Is a Glitch</a>"), <a href="/wiki/Masaaki_Yuasa" title="Masaaki Yuasa">Masaaki Yuasa</a> ("<a href="/wiki/Food_Chain_(Adventure_Time)" title="Food Chain (Adventure Time)">Food Chain</a>"), David Ferguson ("Water Park Prank"), and <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Kristen_Lepore" title="Kristen Lepore">Kristen Lepore</a> ("<a href="/wiki/Bad_Jubies" title="Bad Jubies">Bad Jubies</a>"). Since the first season, the show has also had an art director; <a href="/wiki/Nick_Jennings_(artist)" title="Nick Jennings (artist)">Nick Jennings</a> (seasons 1–6) and Sandra Lee (seasons 6–10).</span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-note5-7"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-note5_7-0">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">282 regular, plus one special. Ten shorts (i.e., mini-episodes roughly two minutes in length) were also produced.</span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-note12-10"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-note12_10-0">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">In its first season, the series was often billed as <i>Adventure Time with Finn &amp; Jake</i><sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-LATimesReview2_8-0"><a href="#cite_note-LATimesReview2-8"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> because the producers were unsure at the time whether they could secure the rights to the simpler title <i>Adventure Time</i>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-9"><a href="#cite_note-9"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-11"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-11">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">Known as HBO Max until 2023.</span>

</li>

About a week to write an episode, a month to storyboard, a few days to record voices, two weeks to put together an animatic, a week to design it, a week to do clean up on the designs, a week to do color design, then it goes overseas and takes about five months to be animated. The rest of the time goes to retakes editing and music and sound design"</a>. SPAN - Lets fetch the section History

In [284]:
# Find the section containing the History content
history_section = soup.find("span", {"id": "History"})

# If the History section exists, get its content
if history_section:
    
    # Get the parent section (usually an <h2> tag)
    history_heading = history_section.find_parent("h2")
    
    # Initialize a list to store content paragraphs
    history_content = []
    
    # Get all sibling elements until the next <h2> tag and extract text
    next_sibling = history_heading.find_next_sibling()
    while next_sibling and next_sibling.name != "h2":
        if next_sibling.name == "p":
            history_content.append(next_sibling.get_text())
        next_sibling = next_sibling.find_next_sibling()
    
    print("History Content:")
    for paragraph in history_content:
        print(paragraph.strip())  # Strip to remove leading and trailing whitespaces
else:
    print("History section not found.")

History section not found.

Section Title: Contents
Section Content: 


Section Title: Premise
Section Content: Adventure Time follows the adventures of a boy named Finn the Human (voiced by Jeremy Shada), and his best friend and adoptive brother Jake the Dog (John DiMaggio), who has magical powers to change shape and size at will. Pendleton Ward, the series' creator, describes Finn as a "fiery little kid with strong morals".[8] Jake, on the other hand, is based on Tripper Harrison, Bill Murray's character in Meatballs. This means that while Jake is somewhat carefree, he will "sit [Finn] down and give him some decent advice if he really needs it".[8] Finn and Jake live in the post-apocalyptic Land of Ooo, which was ravaged by a cataclysmic event known as the "Mushroom War", a nuclear war that destroyed civilization a thousand years before the series' events. Throughout the series, Finn and Jake interact with major characters, including Princess Bubblegum (Hynden Walch), the sovereign of the Candy Kingdom and a sentient piece of gum; the Ice King (Tom Kenny), a menacing but largely misunderstood ice wizard; Marceline the Vampire Queen (Olivia Olson), a thousand-year-old vampire and rock music enthusiast; Lumpy Space Princess (Pendleton Ward), a melodramatic and immature princess made out of "lumps"; BMO (Niki Yang), a sentient video game console-shaped robot that lives with Finn and Jake; and Flame Princess (Jessica DiCicco), a flame elemental and ruler of the Fire Kingdom.[9]: 346 [10][11]


Section Title: Development
Section Content: According to series creator Pendleton Ward, the show's style was influenced by his time attending the California Institute of the Arts (CalArts) and his experiences working as a writer and storyboard artist on The Marvelous Misadventures of Flapjack, a series that ran on Cartoon Network from 2008 until 2010. In an interview with Animation World Network, Ward said he strove to combine Adventure Time's subversive humor with "beautiful" moments, using Hayao Miyazaki's film My Neighbor Totoro as inspiration for the latter.[8] Ward has also named Home Movies and Dr. Katz, Professional Therapist as influences, largely because both shows are "relaxing" and feature "conversational dialogue that feels natural [and is neither] over the top [nor] cartoony and shrill".[12]


Section Title: Broadcast and ratings
Section Content: Each Adventure Time episode is about eleven minutes in length; pairs of episodes are often telecast in order to fill a half-hour program time slot.[116] Before the official debut of the first season, Cartoon Network aired both "Business Time" and "Evicted!" on March 11 and 18, respectively, advertising these showings as "previews" of the series-to-come.[117][118] The show officially debuted with "Slumber Party Panic" on April 5, 2010.[119]


Section Title: Reception
Section Content: "Adventure Time makes me wish I were a kid again, just so I could grow up to be as awesome as the kids who are currently watching Adventure Time will be".


Section Title: Related media
Section Content: On October 23, 2019, Cartoon Network announced that four hour-long specials—collectively titled Adventure Time: Distant Lands—would air on HBO Max. The specials aired in 2020 and 2021. On August 17, 2021, it was announced that a second spin-off, Adventure Time: Fionna and Cake, focusing on the gender-swapped Fionna and Cake characters, had been ordered by HBO Max.[195] On June 12, 2024, it was revealed that two additional spin-offs, entitled Adventure Time: Side Quests and Adventure Time: Heyo BMO, had also been greenlit by Cartoon Network Studios.[196]

# Import TextBlob for sentiment analysis
from textblob import TextBlob

# Sentiment Analysis Function using TextBlob
def sentiment_analysis(text):
    blob = TextBlob(text)
    return blob.sentiment.polarity, blob.sentiment.subjectivity

# Apply sentiment analysis to each section
# Title
title_polarity, title_subjectivity = sentiment_analysis(title)
print(f"\nSentiment of Title -> Polarity: {title_polarity}, Subjectivity: {title_subjectivity}")


# Introductory Paragraph
if 'intro' in locals() and intro:  # Ensure 'intro' is defined
    intro_polarity, intro_subjectivity = sentiment_analysis(intro)
    print(f"\nSentiment of Introduction -> Polarity: {intro_polarity}, Subjectivity: {intro_subjectivity}")
else:
    print("No Introduction content to analyze.")


# History
if 'history_content' in locals() and history_content:  # Ensure history_content is defined and has content
    history_text = ' '.join(history_content)  # Combine paragraphs into a single string for analysis
    history_polarity, history_subjectivity = sentiment_analysis(history_text)
    print(f"\nSentiment of History Section -> Polarity: {history_polarity}, Subjectivity: {history_subjectivity}")
else:
    print("No History content to analyze.")

# Apply sentiment analysis to the Main Content sections
sections = soup.find_all("h2")
for section in sections:
    section_title = section.text
    section_content_tag = section.find_next("p")
    if section_content_tag:
        section_content = section_content_tag.text.strip()
        section_polarity, section_subjectivity = sentiment_analysis(section_content)
        print(f"Sentiment of Section '{section_title}' -> Polarity: {section_polarity}, Subjectivity: {section_subjectivity}")

# Apply sentiment analysis to the References
print("\nAnalyzing References:")
for ref in references_links[:5]:  # Limiting to the first 5 references for brevity
    reference_url = ref.get("href")
    print(f"Reference URL: {reference_url}")

# Extract the external reference links
references_links = soup.find_all("a", {"class": "external text"})
print("References Links Text Sentiment Analysis:")

for link in references_links:
    link_text = link.get_text()  # Extract the text inside the <a> tag
    blob = TextBlob(link_text)   # Perform sentiment analysis
    polarity = blob.sentiment.polarity
    subjectivity = blob.sentiment.subjectivity
    print(f"Link Text: {link_text}")
    print(f"Polarity: {polarity}, Subjectivity: {subjectivity}")
    print("---")

Link Text: "It takes about 8 months to create an episode from start to finish. About a week to write an episode, a month to storyboard, a few days to record voices, two weeks to put together an animatic, a week to design it, a week to do clean up on the designs, a week to do color design, then it goes overseas and takes about five months to be animated. The rest of the time goes to retakes editing and music and sound design"
